```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# loading
if (!require("pacman")) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
pacman::p_load(
  tree, rpart, randomForest, ranger, rattle, pROC,
  partykit, ggplot2, glmnet, lda, data.table,
  stargazer, gridExtra, ggrepel, readr, dplyr, tidyr
)
options(scipen = 0, digits = 3)
```

```{r import-data}
data_path <- "../../data/speed_dating_clean.csv"
data <- readr::read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Select variables by name so the code does not depend on column positions.
target <- "dec"
predictors <- c(
  "gender", "age", "race",
  "age_o", "race_o", "samerace",
  "attr", "sinc", "intel", "fun", "amb", "shar"
)

required_columns <- c(target, predictors)

# data1 is the final modeling data. iid is excluded because it is only a participant identifier.
# data1 changes numerical variables into categorical variables/factors
data1 <- data |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_columns)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dec = factor(dec, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    race = factor(race),
    race_o = factor(race_o),
    samerace = factor(samerace, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  ) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

# dim(data1)
# names(data1)
# table(data1$dec)
```

```{r rf}
# Binary random forest using the OOB error for internal evaluation.
set.seed(1)
fit.rf <- randomForest::randomForest(
  dec ~ .,
  data = data1,
  mtry = 4,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

# names(fit.rf)
```

```{r}
# OOB predictions and OOB classification error
oob_pred <- fit.rf$predicted
oob_error <- mean(oob_pred != data1$dec)

oob_error
table(
  Actual = data1$dec,
  Predicted = oob_pred
)

# OOB classification error as the number of trees increases.
plot(
  fit.rf,
  type = "l",
  col = c("black", "blue", "red"),
  main = "OOB classification error"
)
oob_error <- fit.rf$err.rate[fit.rf$ntree, "OOB"]
oob_error

# OOB confusion matrix and variable importance.
fit.rf$confusion
randomForest::importance(fit.rf)
randomForest::varImpPlot(fit.rf)
```

```{r oob-probabilities}
# OOB probability of a "Yes" decision. For each observation, this probability
# uses votes only from trees that did not use that observation for training.
oob_probability <- fit.rf$votes[, "Yes"]
oob_actual <- data1$dec
oob_actual_yes <- oob_actual == "Yes"
```

```{r roc-curve}
# ROC curve: sensitivity versus false-positive rate across all thresholds.
roc_object <- pROC::roc(
  response = oob_actual,
  predictor = oob_probability,
  levels = c("No", "Yes"),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

plot(
  roc_object,
  legacy.axes = TRUE,
  print.auc = TRUE,
  col = "blue",
  lwd = 2,
  main = "OOB ROC Curve"
)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray50")

roc_auc <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_object))
roc_auc
```

```{r precision-recall-curve}
# PR curve: precision versus recall for the positive ("Yes") class.
# Predictions with the same probability are grouped at one threshold.
pr_curve <- tibble::tibble(
  actual_yes = oob_actual_yes,
  probability = oob_probability
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(probability) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    positive_count = sum(actual_yes),
    negative_count = sum(!actual_yes),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(probability)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    true_positive = cumsum(positive_count),
    false_positive = cumsum(negative_count),
    recall = true_positive / sum(oob_actual_yes),
    precision = true_positive / (true_positive + false_positive)
  )

# Average precision summarizes the PR curve; larger values are better.
average_precision <- sum(
  c(pr_curve$recall[1], diff(pr_curve$recall)) * pr_curve$precision
)

pr_plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(recall = 0, precision = 1),
  dplyr::select(pr_curve, recall, precision)
)

positive_prevalence <- mean(oob_actual_yes)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  pr_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = recall, y = precision)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_step(direction = "hv", color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = positive_prevalence,
    linetype = 2,
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "OOB Precision-Recall Curve",
    subtitle = paste("Average precision =", round(average_precision, 3)),
    x = "Recall",
    y = "Precision"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

average_precision
```

```{r calibration-plot}
# Calibration compares predicted "Yes" probabilities with observed "Yes"
# frequencies. Ten groups of approximately equal size are used.
calibration_data <- tibble::tibble(
  actual_yes = as.numeric(oob_actual_yes),
  predicted_probability = oob_probability
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(bin = dplyr::ntile(predicted_probability, 10)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_predicted_probability = mean(predicted_probability),
    observed_yes_rate = mean(actual_yes),
    observations = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  calibration_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = mean_predicted_probability,
    y = observed_yes_rate
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = 2,
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(size = observations),
    color = "blue",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "OOB Calibration Plot",
    x = "Mean predicted probability",
    y = "Observed Yes rate"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

# Brier score is the mean squared error of the predicted probabilities.
# Smaller values indicate better probabilistic predictions.
brier_score <- mean(
  (oob_probability - as.numeric(oob_actual_yes))^2
)
brier_score
```
